To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synaptic noise is generated by a small number of afferent neurons, and that this is a general phenomenon.
the Mauthner inhibitory networks are not homogeneous and that the stochastic activity of the Mauthner is generated by a subset of its presynaptic cells.

(1) the spectrum of synaptic noise is not a simple power law, as previously thought; (2) it is not the result of a simple superposition of signals from all the afferent cells; (3) it can be generated by a small number of neurons in the presynthetic network; (4) it is not necessary to postulate the existence of a specific noise generator, as has often been proposed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation and propagation of noise in the nervous system.
the generation of stochastic signals in the nervous system.
the generation of synaptic noise and its role in information processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mauthner neuron is subjected to a background of inhibitory noise which is generated by a few subsets of afferents, and that this noise is not a simple Poisson process.
noise is generated by the operation of a small number of cells, but the identity of these cells depends on the particular network.
the Mauthner neuron does not receive synaptic noise from all afferents, but from subsets of afferents only.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Mauthner neuron is a very good example to show how a neuron can be a good integrator of the input signals, but a poor detector of the noise.
synaptic noise is a highly organized process.
synaptic noise is not an intrinsic property of neurons, but a result of the operation of their networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synaptic noise is not a uniform property of the nervous system, but depends on the specific structure of the network in which the target neuron is embedded.
synaptic noise, far from being a uniform background activity, is generated by the operation of specific neuronal circuits.
synaptic noise, which is ubiquitous in the nervous system, is not generated by all cells in an input network but by subsets of them.
